translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled with Qingzhou, he himself led his unit's troops to attack the city and also tried to entice Qiong by letter; Qiong therefore refused him, forwarded the letter to court, and the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled from Qingzhou, Qiong led his troops against the city. Guangyuan tried to win him over by letter, but Qiong refused and sent the letter to court, winning praise.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，改洺州團練使，累官至加檢校司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he was made military training commissioner of Mingzhou and rose through offices to Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun he became military training commissioner of Ming and eventually rose to Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三年，授護聖右廂都指揮使，領岳州團練使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed overall commander of the right wing of the Guarding Sagely Corps with titular command as military training commissioner of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made overall commander of the right wing of the Guarding Sagely Corps and military training commissioner of Yue.

sentences.zh: 時洺州吏民列狀保留，朝廷不允。

translations.literal: At that time the officials and people of Mingzhou submitted a collective petition to retain him; the court did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people of Ming submitted a petition to keep him, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 及杜重威降敵，改授瓊威州刺史。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei surrendered to the enemy, Qiong was reassigned as prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei surrendered to the enemy, Qiong was reassigned prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 行及鄭州，遇群盜攻郡，與方太禦賊，中流矢而卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: While traveling and reaching Zhengzhou he met bandits attacking the commandery; together with Fang Tai he resisted the bandits, was struck by a flying arrow, and died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On the road at Zhengzhou he met bandits attacking the city. He and Fang Tai fought them off, but Qiong was killed by an arrow, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 高漢筠，字時英，齊州歷山人也。

translations.literal: Gao Hanyun, courtesy name Shiying, was a native of Lishan in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hanyun, courtesy name Shiying, was from Lishan in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖詣，嘗為是邑令，故家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi had once been magistrate of that district, and so the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi had once been magistrate of that district, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 漢筠少好書傳，嘗詣長白山講肄，會唐末齊、魯交兵，梁氏方霸，乃擲筆謁焉，尋納於軍門。

translations.literal: In youth Hanyun loved books and the classics; he once went to Mount Changbai to lecture and study. When at the end of Tang Qi and Lu were at war and the Liang house was rising to dominance, he threw down his brush and went to pay court, and soon was enrolled in the army.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Hanyun loved the classics and studied on Mount Changbai. When late Tang saw Qi and Lu at war and Liang was rising, he cast aside his brush, sought service, and soon entered the army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為衛州牙校。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as adjutant of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became adjutant of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，莊宗入魏，分兵諭其屬郡，時漢筠以利病說衛之牧守，俾送款於莊宗，以漢筠為功，尋移洺州都校。

translations.literal: During Tianyou of Tang, Zhuangzong entered Wei and divided troops to instruct the subordinate commanderies. At that time Hanyun used arguments of advantage and harm to persuade Wei's governor to offer submission to Zhuangzong; taking Hanyun's effort as merit, he was soon moved to chief adjutant of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang's Tianyou era Zhuangzong entered Wei and sent troops to summon the subordinate commanderies. Hanyun persuaded Wei's governor to submit by arguing the costs and benefits. For this he was soon made chief adjutant of Ming.

sentences.zh: 其後改常山為北京，以漢筠為皇城使，加檢校兵部尚書、左驍衛將軍同正。

translations.literal: Afterward Changshan was made the Northern Capital; Hanyun was made commissioner of the imperial city and given the ranks of Acting Minister of War and regular general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Changshan became the Northern Capital, Hanyun was made commissioner of the imperial city with the ranks of Acting Minister of War and regular general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，除成德軍節度副使，俄以荊門用軍，促詔漢筠移倅襄州，權知軍州事。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was made deputy military commissioner of the Chengde Army; soon because Jingmen needed troops an urgent edict moved Hanyun to serve as deputy at Xiangzhou with acting authority over military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne he became deputy military commissioner of the Chengde Army. Soon, because Jingmen needed troops, he was urgently transferred to Xiangzhou as deputy with acting authority over military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 長興中，歷曹、亳二州刺史。

translations.literal: During Changxing he served in turn as prefect of Cao and Bo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he served in turn as prefect of Cao and Bo.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，加檢校司徒，行左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was made Acting Minister of Education and acted as great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was made Acting Minister of Education and acting great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，高祖建義於河東，唐末帝遣晉昌節度使張敬達率師圍太原，委漢筠巡撫其郡。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai Gaozu raised the banner of revolt in Hedong; the Last Emperor of Tang sent Zhang Jingda, military commissioner of Jinchang, to lead troops and besiege Taiyuan, and entrusted Hanyun with patrolling and pacifying the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai, when Gaozu rose in Hedong, the Last Emperor of Tang sent Zhang Jingda of Jinchang to besiege Taiyuan and entrusted Hanyun with pacifying the commandery.

sentences.zh: 及敬達遇害，節度副使田承肇率部兵攻漢筠於府署，漢筠乃啟關延承肇，謂曰：「仆與子俱承朝寄，而相迫何甚？

translations.literal: When Jingda was killed, the deputy military commissioner Tian Chengzhao led his unit's troops to attack Hanyun in the government offices. Hanyun then opened the gate and admitted Chengzhao, saying, "You and I alike bear the court's commission—why press me so hard?"
translations.idiomatic: After Jingda was killed, deputy military commissioner Tian Chengzhao attacked Hanyun in the government offices. Hanyun opened the gate and admitted him, saying, "We both serve the court. Why press me so hard?"

sentences.zh: 」承肇曰：「我欲扶公為節度使。

translations.literal: " Chengzhao said, "I wish to set you up as military commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhao said, "I want to make you military commissioner."

sentences.zh: 」澤筠曰：「老夫耄矣，不敢首為亂階，死生系子籌之。

translations.literal: " Hanyun said, "This old man is aged; I dare not be the first to make a ladder of disorder—life and death are in your planning."
translations.idiomatic: Hanyun said, "I am an old man and dare not start a rebellion. My life is in your hands."

sentences.zh: 」承肇目左右令前，諸軍投刃於地，曰：「高金吾累朝宿德，不可枉殺。

translations.literal: " Chengzhao signaled those beside him to advance; the troops threw their blades to the ground and said, "Senior Golden Crow Gao is a man of longstanding merit through many reigns—he must not be killed unjustly."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhao signaled his men forward, but the troops threw down their blades and said, "Senior Golden Crow Gao is a man of merit through many reigns. He must not be killed."

sentences.zh: 」承肇以眾意難拒，遂謝云：「與公戲耳！

translations.literal: " Chengzhao, unable to refuse the troops' will, then apologized, saying, "I was only jesting with you!"
translations.idiomatic: Unable to defy them, Chengzhao apologized and said, "I was only joking!"

sentences.zh: 」漢筠促騎以還。

translations.literal: " Hanyun spurred his horse and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyun spurred his horse and rode back.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，飛詔征之，遇諸途，乃入覲，尋遷左驍衛大將軍、內客省使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he sent a flying edict summoning him; they met on the road, and he then attended court; soon he was moved to great general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he summoned Hanyun by urgent edict. They met on the road, and Hanyun attended court. Soon he became great general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天福三年正月，遘疾，終東京之私第，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Tianfu he fell ill and died at his private residence in the Eastern Capital, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Tianfu he fell ill and died at his home in the Eastern Capital, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 漢筠性寬厚，儀容偉如也。

translations.literal: Hanyun was generous by nature and imposing in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyun was generous by nature and imposing in bearing.

sentences.zh: 雖歷戎職，未嘗有非法之言出於口吻，多慕士大夫所為，復以清白自負。

translations.literal: Although he passed through military offices, no unlawful word ever left his lips; he greatly admired what scholar-officials did and also prided himself on integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Though he spent his career in military office, no unlawful word ever left his lips. He admired scholar-officials and prided himself on integrity.

sentences.zh: 在襄陽，有孽吏常課外獻白金二十鎰，漢筠曰：「非多納枿泬，則刻削阛鋏，吾有正俸，此何用焉！

translations.literal: At Xiangyang a corrupt clerk regularly levied extra tribute of twenty ingots of white silver. Hanyun said, "Unless you collect more corrupt surcharges or squeeze market tolls, what use is this to me? I have my regular salary!"
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang a corrupt clerk regularly offered twenty ingots of silver as extra tribute. Hanyun said, "Unless you squeeze the people with corrupt levies or market tolls, where does this come from? I have my regular salary. What do I need this for?"

sentences.zh: 」因戒其主者不復然，其白金皆以狀上進，有詔嘉之。

translations.literal: " He therefore warned the chief clerk not to do so again; all the white silver was submitted upward in a written report, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He warned the chief clerk never to do so again, reported all the silver to court, and received an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 及蒞濟陰，部民安之，四邑飯僧凡有萬八千人。

translations.literal: When he arrived at Jiyin the people of his department were at peace; in four districts he fed monks totaling eighteen thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: When he took office at Jiyin the people were at peace. In four districts he fed eighteen thousand monks.

sentences.zh: 在亳州三年，歲以己俸百千代納逋租，斯亦近代之良二千石也。

translations.literal: During three years at Bozhou he each year used a hundred thousand of his own salary to pay overdue rents on the people's behalf—truly a fine prefect of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: During three years at Bo he each year used a hundred thousand of his own salary to pay overdue rents for the people. He was truly one of the fine prefects of recent times.

sentences.zh: 長子貞文，仕皇朝，為開封少尹，卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhenwen served the imperial dynasty as vice intendant of Kaifeng and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhenwen served the dynasty as vice intendant of Kaifeng and died in office.

sentences.zh: 彥韜出於軍旅，植性和厚，理綿州日，甚著綏懷之譽，故有賞典旌焉。

translations.literal: Yantao came from the military ranks; his nature was mild and generous. While governing Mianzhou he won great renown for soothing and cherishing the people, and therefore received commendatory rewards and banners of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yantao came from the army, and his nature was mild and generous. While governing Mian he won great renown for soothing the people and received commendatory rewards.

sentences.zh: 在濮陽，屬清泰末，群寇入郡，郡人大擾，彥韜率帳下百人，一呼破之，人皆感之。

translations.literal: At Puyang, late in Qingtai when bandits entered the commandery and the people were greatly disturbed, Yantao led a hundred men from his tent, broke them with one shout, and everyone was moved with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: At Puyang, late in Qingtai, when bandits entered the commandery and threw the people into panic, Yantao led a hundred of his personal troops and routed them with one charge. The people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 但不能守廉養正，以終令譽。

translations.literal: Yet he could not maintain integrity and cultivate rectitude to the end of his fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: But he could not preserve his integrity to the end, and his fine reputation did not last.

sentences.zh: 長興中，罷密州赴闕，苞苴甚厚。

translations.literal: During Changxing, when he left Mizhou and came to court, his gifts and bribes were very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing, when he left Mi and came to court, he brought lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 起甲第於洛陽，逾月而成，華堂廣廡，亞王公之家，見者嗤之。

translations.literal: He built a grand mansion in Luoyang that was finished in little more than a month—splendid halls and broad corridors rivaling the houses of princes and dukes, and those who saw it mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: He built a grand mansion in Luoyang in little more than a month, with splendid halls and broad corridors rivaling princely residences. Those who saw it mocked him.

sentences.zh: 故淹翔五郡，位不及廉察，抑有由也。

translations.literal: Therefore he lingered through five commanderies yet never reached the rank of surveillance commissioner—there was reason for it after all.
translations.idiomatic: That is why he served in five commanderies yet never rose to surveillance commissioner. There was reason for it.

sentences.zh: 李彥珣，邢州人也。

translations.literal: Li Yanxun was a native of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanxun was from Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少為郡之牙吏。

translations.literal: In youth he was an adjutant of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was a commandery adjutant.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，明宗鎮其地，彥珣素無檢節，因洽於左右，明宗即位，以為通事舍人。

translations.literal: During Tianyou of Tang, when Mingzong held that territory, Yanxun had always lacked restraint; he cultivated those at Mingzong's side, and when Mingzong took the throne he was made courier-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang's Tianyou era, when Mingzong governed the region, Yanxun was unrestrained and cultivated Mingzong's attendants. When Mingzong took the throne he made Yanxun courier-attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣使東川，行至其境，其仆從為董璋所收，彥珣竄還，以失敬故也。

translations.literal: He was once sent as envoy to Dongchuan; when he reached its border his attendants were seized by Dong Zhang, and Yanxun fled back—for lack of respect.
translations.idiomatic: He was once sent as envoy to Dongchuan. When he reached the border Dong Zhang seized his attendants, and Yanxun fled back in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 朝廷攻璋，詔授行營步軍都監。

translations.literal: When the court attacked Zhang, an edict appointed him overall monitor of the campaign infantry.
translations.idiomatic: When the court attacked Zhang, he was made overall monitor of the campaign infantry.

sentences.zh: 彥珣素不孝於父母，在鄉絕其供饋，同列惡其鄙惡，旋出為外任。

translations.literal: Yanxun had always been unfilial toward his parents and cut off their support while in his home district; his colleagues detested his baseness, and he was soon sent out to an external post.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxun had long been unfilial and cut off his parents' support at home. His colleagues despised his baseness, and he was soon sent to an outside post.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，遷河陽行軍司馬，遇張從賓為亂，因朋助之，從賓敗，奔於魏州。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he was moved to acting military secretary of Heyang; when Zhang Congbin rebelled he joined him as an accomplice; when Congbin was defeated he fled to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he became acting military secretary of Heyang. When Zhang Congbin rebelled he joined him. After Congbin's defeat he fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 範延光既叛，署為步軍都監，委以守陴。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang rebelled he appointed Yanxun overall monitor of the infantry and entrusted him with defending the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang rebelled he made Yanxun overall monitor of the infantry and entrusted him with defending the walls.

sentences.zh: 招討使楊光遠以彥珣見用，欲撓延光而誘彥珣，乃遣人就邢臺訪得其母，令於城下以招之。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner Yang Guangyuan, because Yanxun was employed, wished to shake Yanguang and entice Yanxun; he therefore sent someone to Xingtai to find his mother and had her call to him from below the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Yang Guangyuan, wishing to undermine Yanguang, sent men to Xingtai to find Yanxun's mother and had her call to him from below the wall.

sentences.zh: 彥珣識其母，發矢以斃之，見者傷之。

translations.literal: Yanxun recognized his mother, shot an arrow, and killed her; those who saw it were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxun recognized his mother, shot her dead with an arrow, and all who saw it were horrified.

sentences.zh: 及隨延光出降，授坊州刺史。

translations.literal: When he followed Yanguang out to surrender he was appointed prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he surrendered with Yanguang he was made prefect of Fang.

sentences.zh: 近臣以彥珣之惡逆奏於高祖，高祖曰：「赦命已行，不可改也。

translations.literal: Intimate ministers reported Yanxun's wicked rebellion to Gaozu. Gaozu said, "The amnesty has already been issued and cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Intimate ministers reported Yanxun's crimes to Gaozu. Gaozu said, "The amnesty has already been issued and cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 」遂令赴郡，後不知其所終焉。

translations.literal: " He therefore ordered him to go to his commandery; later no one knew how he ended.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yanxun to take up his post. Later no one knew his end.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》云：彥珣後以坐贓誅。）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang Xiu's History records: Yanxun was later executed for corruption.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang Xiu's History records that Yanxun was later executed for corruption.)]

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔從簡從莊宗戰於河上，可謂勇矣，及其為末帝守於孟津，豈得為忠乎？

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In former days Congjian fought with Zhuangzong along the Yellow River—one may call that courage; yet when he held Mengjin for the Last Emperor, how can that be called loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Congjian fought with Zhuangzong along the Yellow River—that was courage. But when he held Mengjin for the Last Emperor, where was the loyalty?

sentences.zh: 忠既無聞，勇何足貴！

translations.literal: With no loyalty to speak of, what is courage worth!
translations.idiomatic: Without loyalty, what is courage worth?

sentences.zh: 潘環、方太，雖鹹負雄幹，而俱歿亂世，蓋方略不足以衛其身故也。

translations.literal: Pan Huan and Fang Tai, though both possessed imposing stature, both perished in chaotic times—probably because their strategy was insufficient to preserve their persons.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Huan and Fang Tai were imposing men, yet both died in chaotic times—probably because their strategy was not enough to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 何建舉秦、隴之封，附巴、邛之俗，守方之寄，其若是乎！

translations.literal: He Jian raised the seals of Qin and Long, attached himself to the customs of Ba and Qiong—is this what is meant by the charge to guard a frontier!
translations.idiomatic: He Jian took the seals of Qin and Long and attached himself to the ways of Ba and Qiong—is that what guarding a frontier means?

sentences.zh: 其餘皆儋珪析爵之流也，亦可以垂名於是矣。

translations.literal: The rest were of the sort who held fragmented fiefs and divided noble ranks—yet they too could leave their names in the record.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were men who held splintered fiefs and divided noble ranks—yet they too could leave their names on record.

sentences.zh: 秘瓊既覆董氏之族，旋為鄴帥所屠，何報應之速也！

translations.literal: Mi Qiong had already destroyed the Dong clan, and was soon slaughtered by the military commissioner of Ye—how swift the retribution!
translations.idiomatic: Mi Qiong destroyed the Dong clan and was soon slaughtered by the commander of Ye. How swift the retribution!

sentences.zh: 惟彥珣忍射其親，殆非人類，晉祖宥之不戮，蓋失刑之甚也。

translations.literal: Only Yanxun could bear to shoot his own kin—hardly human. That Jin Zu spared him and did not execute him was surely a grave failure of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanxun could shoot his own mother—barely human at all. That Jin Zu spared him was a grave failure of justice.
